narrativeReportMd:
# ClaimResponse R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found in local `ClaimResponse` content. The highest-impact changes are the required `patient` to `subject` rename with a new `Group` target, adjudication non-money values changing from decimal `value` to `Quantity` `quantity`, remodeling of added-item body-site data, and process-note representation changes. R6 also relaxes several R4-required cardinalities and adds substantial optional content, creating important R6-to-R4 representability risks.

## Scope
The comparison used the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions plus package indexes, metadata, and selected local terminology artifacts. Inherited-only base changes from `Element`, `Resource`, `DomainResource`, and datatypes are excluded from findings and listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration is mostly a structural transform rather than simple terminology substitution: required recipient data must move from `patient` to `subject`; adjudication and body-site substructures need JSON reshaping; process-note type handling must move from primitive codes to CodeableConcepts; and R6-only optional fields need an extension or loss policy for R4 export.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `patient` -> `subject`, adjudication `value` -> `quantity`, added-item body-site remodeling, and `processNote.type` changing to CodeableConcept. These affect validation, generated code, FHIRPath paths, serializers, and financial business logic.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed where R6 data cannot be deterministically reduced to R4: Group subjects, Quantity units for adjudication values, BodyStructure references or multiple body-site groups, local language codes, missing R4-required data, and R6-only adjudication/supporting/error details.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some changes are justified by more expressive modeling, but several could have been phased with deprecated aliases or parallel optional fields. Optional additions are forward-compatible but still require a deliberate R6-to-R4 preservation strategy.

## Follow-up analysis
Base artifact reports should cover inherited `DomainResource`, `Element`, and datatype changes. Terminology expansion and official cross-version maps would improve confidence for language and outcome terminology and for structural conversions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ClaimResponse has multiple local hard breaks: required `patient` became required `subject`, adjudication non-money values became `Quantity`, added-item body sites were remodeled, and process-note type changed representation. The top R6-to-R4 uncertainty is how to preserve new R6 optional content and richer datatypes without official cross-version maps.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The migration themes are path renaming, object-shape replacement, richer datatypes, relaxed R6 cardinalities, and additive R6-only content. R4-to-R6 migration needs deterministic transforms for recipient, adjudication, body-site, and process-note fields. R6-to-R4 migration needs explicit loss policies or extensions for Group subjects, Quantity units, BodyStructure references, optional R6 additions, and records omitting R4-required elements.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and cardinality findings because both StructureDefinition snapshots were available and matched at the same canonical resource identity. Confidence is medium for terminology nuance because local ValueSet/CodeSystem files were inspected but no live terminology expansion, official diff, or ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: Mandatory ClaimResponse.patient was replaced by mandatory ClaimResponse.subject and the target domain widened to Group

semanticText.short: The recipient of the products and services
semanticText.definition: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual or forecast reimbursement is sought.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 the recipient was represented by the required `patient` element, and the only allowed target was `Patient`.

semanticText.short: The recipient(s) of the products and services
semanticText.definition: The party/group to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual or forecast reimbursement is sought.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses the broader `subject` name and permits either an individual `Patient` or a `Group`.

facts.note: The R6 element is a rename plus a target-domain widening.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements have the same cardinality, summary flag, recipient semantics, and nearly identical definitions except for R6 adding group language. The path name changed from `patient` to `subject`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct JSON path and generated-model break. An R4 instance containing required `patient` does not satisfy R6 because `patient` is no longer defined and required `subject` is missing. In the other direction, an R6 `subject` that references a `Group` has no valid R4 target because R4 only allowed `Patient`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The recipient drives coverage, adjudication context, and reimbursement. A failed or lossy patient/subject mapping can attach a response to the wrong beneficiary or make the record unprocessable.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize ClaimResponse so the recipient can be an individual or group while aligning with broader FHIR subject naming.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the required `patient` path, broaden its target to `Patient|Group`, and update its definition/aliases to recipient or subject semantics.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing the ClaimResponse recipient to include `Group` is a reasonable R6 goal. The hard break comes from renaming a required element that already represented the recipient. Because the same recipient generalization could have been achieved by keeping the R4 path and broadening the target, the breaking rename looks probably avoidable rather than necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `ClaimResponse.patient` as `1..1`, widen its allowed target profiles to `Patient` and `Group`, and clarify in the definition that the element identifies the recipient/subject. That preserves existing R4 instances and supports group recipients. The cost is living with a nonoptimal field name for group cases; adding a new parallel `subject` field would introduce duplicate recipient representations, but simple target widening avoids that duplication.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve R4 instances with low validation cost; the main tradeoff is a misleading legacy element name and weaker consistency with subject-named resources.

evidence.detail: R4 has required `ClaimResponse.patient` with type `Reference(Patient)`.
R6 has required `ClaimResponse.subject` with target profiles `Patient` and `Group`.
The R4 `patient` element is absent from the R6 snapshot.
R6 definition explicitly says the recipient may be a party or group.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative. The R4-to-R6 transform is straightforward only when `patient` references a Patient. R6 `Group` subjects require a policy decision because R4 has no equivalent target.

findings.narrativeMd: `ClaimResponse.patient` is not merely renamed; it becomes `ClaimResponse.subject` and the allowable target set expands to include `Group`. This will break strict JSON validation and generated R4 client code that reads or writes `patient`. It also introduces a real cross-version mapping problem for R6 group-level claim responses.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid data with `patient` and no `subject` is invalid against the R6 StructureDefinition because the required R6 element is absent and the old element is unknown. R6 data with `subject.reference = "Group/..."` cannot be represented as valid R4 without an extension or out-of-band policy because R4 requires a `Patient` reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `patient` to `subject` for Patient recipients and update generated models, FHIRPath, search/extraction logic, tests, and serializers. Add explicit tests for Patient and Group recipients. For Group subjects, choose a cross-version extension, reject for R4 export, or map to a representative Patient only under a documented business rule.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The subject generalization is understandable, but changing the required element name makes every conformant R4 instance require transformation. A backward-compatible deprecation strategy could have reduced disruption while the group-recipient use case matured.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is most important for R6 group subjects and for trading partners that key business rules on beneficiary patient identity.

findings.title: Adjudication non-monetary value changed from decimal `value` to `Quantity` `quantity`

oldState.summary: R4 represented non-monetary adjudication values as optional decimal `value`.

semanticText.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.
semanticText.comment: For example: eligible percentage or co-payment percentage.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used a bare decimal at `item.adjudication.value` for percentages and other non-money adjudication values.

newState.summary: R6 uses optional `quantity` with type `Quantity` for the same non-monetary adjudication concept.

semanticText.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.
semanticText.comment: For example: eligible percentage or co-payment percentage.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves the human definition but changes both the property name and the JSON shape by using `Quantity`.

facts.note: The adjudication backbone is reused by detail, subDetail, addItem, addItem.detail, addItem.detail.subDetail, and header adjudication through content references.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 elements share the same short text, definition, comment, requirements, and parent adjudication backbone; only the element name and type changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 adjudication using `value` will fail R6 validation because the element was removed. R6 `quantity` is an object with optional units, code, system, comparator, and value; it cannot be losslessly represented by the single R4 decimal without a convention.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Percentages and non-money adjudication values can affect allowed amounts, patient responsibility, and benefit calculations. Dropping units or interpreting a fraction as a percent can change financial outcomes.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent non-monetary adjudication values with units and richer Quantity semantics rather than a unitless decimal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated decimal `value` while adding optional `quantity` for richer unit-bearing adjudication values.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using `Quantity` for non-monetary adjudication values is a reasonable modeling improvement because percentages, counts, and unit-bearing values are safer when units can be carried explicitly. A less-breaking overlap was possible, but it would materially complicate validation and interpretation of financial adjudication data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `item.adjudication.value` as a deprecated decimal and added `item.adjudication.quantity`, perhaps with an invariant discouraging both. That would let R4 instances validate while enabling richer R6 data. The tradeoff is long-lived duplicate representations of the same adjudication fact, ambiguity about whether `80` means 80 percent or another unitless quantity, and implementation burden for conflict handling across all reused adjudication backbones.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A dual-field transition would preserve old instances but create duplicate representations and require precedence/conflict rules when both fields appear.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `value` as `decimal` with cardinality `0..1`.
R6 defines `quantity` as `Quantity` with cardinality `0..1` and the same non-monetary value definition.
R4 reuses the adjudication backbone from detail, addItem, subDetail, and header adjudication locations.
R6 reuses the same adjudication backbone from the corresponding locations, so the shape change propagates through those repeated structures.

examples.examplesMd: A simple decimal can be mechanically moved to `quantity.value`, but units such as `%` need local assumptions or adjudication-category-specific rules.

findings.narrativeMd: The adjudication non-money value moved from a primitive decimal to a Quantity object. This affects all places that reuse the adjudication backbone, not just top-level line items. Systems that deserialize `value` as a number or calculate benefit percentages must be updated to understand `quantity` and any unit metadata.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing `item.adjudication.value` or the same reused element under detail/addItem/header adjudication are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 instances using `quantity` are not losslessly R4-representable when the Quantity carries units, system, code, comparator, or extensions beyond the numeric value.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform `value` to `quantity.value` and, where possible, infer a unit from `adjudication.category` or trading-partner rules. Add tests for percentages, unitless quantities, and round-tripping back to R4. Avoid silently discarding `Quantity.unit`, `system`, `code`, or comparator on R6-to-R4 export.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer type is likely justified by better modeling, but a one-release overlap could have avoided immediate instance breakage. Without a supplied ConceptMap or narrative migration note, unit assignment must be resolved by implementers.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review category-specific conventions before converting bare decimals to percentages or other units.

findings.title: ClaimResponse.addItem body-site data was remodeled from flat CodeableConcept fields to repeated backbone entries

oldState.summary: R4 had `addItem.bodySite` as `CodeableConcept` `0..1` and sibling `addItem.subSite` as `CodeableConcept` `0..*`.

binding.description: The code for the teeth, quadrant, sextant and arch.

semanticText.definition: Physical service site on the patient (limb, tooth, etc.).
semanticText.comment: For example: Providing a tooth code allows an insurer to identify a provider performing a filling on a tooth that was previously removed.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented an added item anatomical site as one coded body site and zero or more sibling sub-sites.

newState.summary: R6 makes `addItem.bodySite` a repeating BackboneElement. Each repetition has required `site` `1..*` as `CodeableReference(BodyStructure)` and nested `subSite` `0..*`.

semanticText.definition: Physical location where the service is performed or applies.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 supports multiple body-site groups and each group can use coded references or actual `BodyStructure` references through `CodeableReference`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 nested `bodySite.site` carries the R4 bodySite definition/comment and uses the same tooth value set; R6 `bodySite.subSite` carries the R4 subSite semantics and surface value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changed. R4 `addItem.bodySite` as a CodeableConcept is invalid where R6 expects an array of backbone objects. R4 `addItem.subSite` is removed. R6 can carry multiple site groups and BodyStructure references, which cannot be flattened into the single R4 bodySite plus global subSite list without possible loss of grouping and reference details.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dental, device, and procedure adjudication may depend on exact tooth/surface/body-structure location. Losing site/sub-site grouping can change billing or clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple anatomical locations and references to BodyStructure while keeping sub-sites associated with a specific site.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add the new repeated detailed body-site backbone while retaining deprecated flat `bodySite` and `subSite` aliases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 remodel addresses real R4 limitations: one flat body site, sibling sub-sites not structurally tied to a site, and no native `BodyStructure` reference. A compatibility-preserving overlap was possible, but the duplicate same-resource location model would be materially ambiguous and costly to keep interoperable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have preserved the R4 flat `addItem.bodySite` and `addItem.subSite` fields and added a new detailed repeating structure for multiple sites, grouped sub-sites, and `BodyStructure` references. That would avoid invalidating old instances. The cost is two ways to express the same anatomical fact, unclear precedence when both are populated, and a high risk that deprecated flat fields remain indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping both shapes would preserve old data but create duplicated anatomical-location semantics, precedence questions, and possible loss of site/sub-site grouping discipline.

evidence.detail: R4 `bodySite` is `CodeableConcept` `0..1` with the tooth example value set.
R4 `subSite` is a sibling `CodeableConcept` `0..*` with the surface example value set.
R6 `bodySite` is a repeating BackboneElement.
R6 requires one or more `site` values per bodySite repetition using `CodeableReference(BodyStructure)`.
R6 nests `subSite` under each bodySite repetition.

examples.examplesMd: The exact CodeableReference JSON shape depends on the R6 datatype representation. The important migration point is to wrap the former site code under a bodySite repetition and preserve subSite grouping.

findings.narrativeMd: `ClaimResponse.addItem.bodySite` changed from a single CodeableConcept to a repeated backbone structure with mandatory nested `site`; `addItem.subSite` moved under that structure. This is a hard break for serializers and generated classes and also changes the data model from flat to grouped anatomical locations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances that contain `addItem.bodySite` as a CodeableConcept or `addItem.subSite` as a sibling element become invalid in R6. R6 instances with multiple body-site groups or BodyStructure references are not losslessly representable in R4, which has only one coded body site and a flat list of sub-sites.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform R4 `bodySite` into one R6 `bodySite` repetition with `site.concept`; move sibling `subSite` values into that repetition. For R6-to-R4, flatten only when there is a single coded site and no BodyStructure reference; otherwise use an extension, reject export, or require human review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The model improvement is clear, but the same goal could have been introduced as an additional optional repeating detailed structure while deprecating the flat fields. The chosen design favors a cleaner R6 model over direct backward compatibility.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the exact CodeableReference JSON conventions used by target tooling before implementing transforms.

findings.title: ClaimResponse.processNote.type changed from primitive code to CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 `processNote.type` was optional primitive `code` bound required to note-type version 4.0.1.

semanticText.definition: The business purpose of the note text.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serialized note purpose as a scalar code such as `"display"`.

newState.summary: R6 `processNote.type` is optional `CodeableConcept` bound extensible to note-type.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local CodeSystem concepts inspected in the package remain `display`, `print`, and `printoper`; the material break is representation, not known code removal.

semanticText.definition: The business purpose of the note text.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 serializes note purpose as a CodeableConcept, allowing coding systems, display text, and extensions beyond a primitive code.

facts.note: Codes inspected in local CodeSystem files are stable.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON representation changes from a primitive string token to an object. R4 instances with `processNote.type` will not validate as R6 without wrapping the code in a CodeableConcept. R6 CodeableConcepts with multiple codings, text-only values, or non-note-type codings cannot be reduced to a single R4 required code without loss or policy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Process notes can direct display, printing, and operational handling. Mis-mapping note purpose can hide information from the intended audience.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer and locally coded note-purpose metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated primitive `type` and add a parallel CodeableConcept element for richer note-purpose coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving note purpose from a primitive code to `CodeableConcept` is a reasonable way to support coded systems, display text, translations, and extensions. The old primitive cannot carry that richer metadata. A less-breaking additive approach exists, but it has material duplicate-representation and conflict-resolution costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `processNote.type` as the deprecated primitive code and added a new optional `processNote.typeCodeableConcept` or equivalent. R4 instances with `type: "print"` would remain valid, while richer R6 coding could use the new element. The tradeoff is two same-resource note-purpose representations, ambiguity when both are present, and extra converter logic to select a single R4 code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The overlap would preserve R4 note codes but create duplicate note-purpose fields and require rules for precedence and down-conversion.

evidence.detail: R4 type is primitive `code` with required note-type binding.
R6 type is `CodeableConcept` with extensible note-type binding.
Local R4 and R6 note-type CodeSystems both contain `display`, `print`, and `printoper`.

processNote.text: Print this explanation on the remittance advice.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-to-R6 transform can wrap known R4 codes in a CodeableConcept. R6-to-R4 requires selecting one coding and rejecting or extending cases that do not contain an R4 note-type code.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.type` is a serialization and codegen break. Existing R4 parsers expect a scalar code and R6 parsers expect a CodeableConcept. The code list appears stable, so the problem is the representation and the broader R6 coding space, not a removed note-purpose code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `"type":"print"` is invalid in R6 because the element type is no longer primitive `code`. An R6 CodeableConcept can be valid without a single R4 note-type code, so down-conversion may be lossy or impossible.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 codes into a CodeableConcept using the note-type code system. Update generated models, serializers, and UI/business logic that switch on string values. For R6-to-R4, require exactly one recognized note-type code or preserve richer content in an extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer type is reasonable but could have been introduced as an additive element. The direct type replacement makes optional note metadata a hard validation break when present.

findings.title: ClaimResponse.processNote.text changed from string to markdown

oldState.summary: R4 required process note text as primitive `string`.

semanticText.definition: The explanation or description associated with the processing.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 note text was a plain FHIR string.

newState.summary: R6 requires process note text as primitive `markdown`.

semanticText.definition: The explanation or description associated with the processing.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 note text is a markdown primitive, still serialized as a JSON string but with markdown semantics and generated type changes.

facts.note: The wire primitive remains a JSON string; the FHIR primitive type changes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The local primitive type changed, so generated classes and schema metadata change. However, `markdown` is based on `string` and the local primitive definitions inspected use the same broad string regex in R6, so most R4 string values should remain wire-valid. Runtime behavior can still change if renderers interpret markdown syntax.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is display/rendering changes, such as markdown formatting characters becoming active presentation markup.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `processNote.text` as `string` and update the definition/comment to say markdown syntax is permitted.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Formatted explanatory notes are a reasonable goal, and this change is not a hard JSON instance break because both primitives serialize as strings. However, the formal type replacement still creates type-aware codegen and rendering churn. The same practical goal could mostly be met by retaining `string` and clarifying markdown usage, so the break is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep the R4 `string` type and add normative text that the value may contain GitHub-flavored Markdown. Existing instances and generated string properties would continue to work, while systems that want formatted display could opt in based on the definition. The cost is weaker machine-readable signaling: validators and generic renderers could not infer markdown handling solely from the primitive type.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves wire and generated-type compatibility; the tradeoff is losing a computable datatype signal that renderers and validators can use to recognize markdown.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `string` and cardinality is `1..1`.
R6 type is `markdown` and cardinality remains `1..1`.
R6 `markdown` derives from `string`; no narrower local regex was found in the inspected primitive definition.

examples.examplesMd: The same JSON string can usually be carried forward, but display tests should cover markdown-sensitive characters such as `*`, `_`, links, and line breaks.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.text` now advertises markdown semantics. This is unlikely to make ordinary R4 strings invalid, but it can affect generated models, primitive type switches, validation metadata, and display rendering.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a typical old-valid/new-invalid JSON break because both primitives serialize as strings. The compatibility risk is runtime and semantic: code that treats the field as plain text may render or sanitize differently when the FHIR type is markdown.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Keep the string value, update type mappings to markdown, and test UI rendering/sanitization for markdown syntax. If systems must preserve plain-text display, escape or render according to local policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Using markdown is a precision improvement, but it could also have been documented without changing the primitive type. The chosen approach favors explicit semantics over codegen stability.

findings.title: ClaimResponse.processNote.language binding strengthened from preferred common languages to required all BCP-47 languages

oldState.summary: R4 optional CodeableConcept with preferred binding to common languages.

semanticText.definition: A code to define the language used in the text of the note.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, non-common or local language codings could still be instance-valid because the binding was only preferred.

newState.summary: R6 optional CodeableConcept with required binding to all BCP-47 languages.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 value set includes all possible BCP-47 codes and has a starter binding to common languages. A full expansion was not performed.

semanticText.definition: A code to define the language used in the text of the note.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires language codings to come from the all-languages BCP-47 value set.

facts.note: Value set scope widened while binding strength increased.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The strength increase changes validation behavior: R4 instances using a local, non-BCP-47, or otherwise unrecognized process-note language coding could be valid with only a preferred-binding warning but invalid in R6. The value set also widens from common languages to all BCP-47 languages, so conformant BCP-47 languages outside the old common set should be supported.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect language tagging can affect display, translation, and patient/provider understanding of explanatory adjudication notes.

justification.inferredGoal: Require interoperable BCP-47 language tags while allowing the full language space.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a preferred or extensible language binding and add best-practice guidance or warning-level validation for BCP-47 tags.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring BCP-47 language tags is a reasonable interoperability goal, and R6 uses the broad all-languages value set rather than only common languages. The less-breaking alternative would tolerate local or informal codes, but that materially weakens the goal of reliably machine-readable language tags for human-facing adjudication notes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept the R4 preferred binding and added guidance or a warning invariant recommending `urn:ietf:bcp:47` codings. That would preserve R4 instances that used local language systems. It is only a partial alternative because systems could still exchange process notes whose language is not enforceably BCP-47, undermining display, translation, and accessibility workflows.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve legacy local language codes but would not provide enforceable base-resource interoperability for process-note language tagging.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred to `ValueSet/languages`.
R6 binding strength is required to `ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4`.
Local value set metadata shows R4 common languages and R6 all possible BCP-47 codes; no full terminology expansion was performed.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates a local code that a preferred binding could tolerate but a required BCP-47 binding should reject. The exact result depends on terminology-service behavior for CodeableConcept required bindings.

findings.narrativeMd: `processNote.language` changed from guidance to enforceable terminology. This is locally scoped to ClaimResponse process notes and is distinct from the inherited DomainResource `language` binding change, which this report excludes from findings.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with omitted `processNote.language` remain valid because the element is optional. Instances with non-BCP-47 or local language codings may become invalid in R6 because the required binding must be satisfied. R6 BCP-47 language codings remain representable in R4 because R4 used a weaker preferred binding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize process-note language codings to BCP-47 (`urn:ietf:bcp:47`) before R6 validation. Inventory local language systems and create a small mapping table. Add tests for omitted language, common language, uncommon but valid BCP-47 language, and invalid local code.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter binding is justifiable for interoperability but could have been phased in with best-practice warnings. Because language tagging affects human comprehension, reject-or-map behavior should be explicit rather than silent.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium because a full terminology expansion/validation of all BCP-47 behavior was not performed.

findings.title: Several R4-required ClaimResponse elements are optional in R6, creating R6-to-R4 validity gaps

affectedLocation.oldPath: ClaimResponse.insurer; ClaimResponse.item.adjudication; ClaimResponse.addItem.productOrService; related addItem/detail adjudication paths

oldState.summary: R4 required insurer and required adjudication/product codes in several nested structures.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 cardinalities included `insurer` `1..1`, `item.adjudication` `1..*`, `item.detail.adjudication` `1..*`, `addItem.adjudication` `1..*`, `addItem.detail.adjudication` `1..*`, `addItem.detail.subDetail.adjudication` `1..*`, and added-item product/service codes `1..1` at addItem/detail/subDetail levels.

newState.summary: R6 relaxes those minimum cardinalities to optional (`0..1` or `0..*`).
newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits ClaimResponses without an insurer and allows item/addItem structures that omit adjudication or product/service codes in places where R4 required them.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Minimum-cardinality decreases are not R4-to-R6 validation breaks. They are significant for reverse conversion: valid R6 data may omit fields that R4 requires, and a converter cannot safely invent insurer, adjudication, or product/service codes without business rules.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Inventing missing financial adjudication data can misstate the payer, service, or benefit decision. Rejecting such records may interrupt historical exchange.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow partially adjudicated, queued, or administratively incomplete responses.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: lowering minimum cardinalities preserves R4-to-R6 instances; the issue is R6-to-R4 representability when R6 omits fields R4 required.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue: R4 instances that populated the required fields remain compatible on these cardinalities. The change creates important R6-to-R4 gaps, but if R6 intends the base resource to admit partial or not-yet-fully-adjudicated responses, decreasing the base minimums is the direct way to do that.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative to assess for this finding. Keeping the R4 `1..1` or `1..*` minimums would improve reverse conversion but would prevent valid base R6 instances from omitting insurer, adjudication, or product/service data. Profiles cannot generally relax a stricter base minimum, so profile guidance would not meet the same base-resource goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Relaxed base cardinalities create reverse-conversion gaps, but retaining R4 minimums would fail the inferred goal of allowing partial, queued, or incomplete base R6 responses.

evidence.detail: R4 `insurer` minimum is 1.
R6 `insurer` minimum is 0.
R4 line-item adjudication minimum is 1.
R6 line-item adjudication minimum is 0.
R4 added-item product/service code minimum is 1 at addItem, detail, and subDetail levels.
R6 added-item product/service code minimum is 0 at addItem, detail, and subDetail levels.

examples.examplesMd: Even after a normal R6 `subject` to R4 `patient` rename, the example lacks R4-required insurer, item adjudication, and added-item product/service details.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes several previously mandatory ClaimResponse data points optional. This is not a forward validation problem for R4 data, but it is a major reverse-conversion issue and may change application assumptions that insurer or adjudication data is always present.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances remain compatible on these specific cardinalities because they contain the fields. R6-valid instances can be R4-invalid if they omit fields whose R4 minimum was 1. Generated R6 models may expose nullable collections or fields where R4-era business logic assumed presence.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 export, validate that required R4 fields are present after other transforms. Do not synthesize payer, adjudication, or product/service codes unless a profile or trading-partner rule supplies deterministic values. Add tests for queued/error responses and addItem entries with omitted product/service.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The relaxations may be necessary for partial workflows, but they shift responsibility to profiles and converters. A profile-based relaxation would have preserved a stricter base resource but reduced R6 flexibility.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review with financial-management domain experts to determine when omitted adjudication/product data is expected versus incomplete.

findings.title: R6 adds substantial optional ClaimResponse content with no native R4 representation

affectedLocation.newPath: ClaimResponse.traceNumber; statusReason; decision; event; encounter; diagnosisRelatedGroup; supportingInfo; reviewOutcome; addItem.request/revenue/category/tax/productOrServiceEnd; error.expression; processNote.class

oldState.summary: R4 lacked these optional local elements and backbone structures.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 ClaimResponse did not have native fields for trace numbers, status reason, adjudication decision, event dates, encounters, diagnosis-related group, supporting information, review outcomes, request links on added items, product/service ranges, taxes, error expressions, or process note class.

newState.summary: R6 adds numerous optional elements across header, item, addItem, processNote, and error structures.
newState.narrativeMd: These additions are optional for R4-to-R6 validation but can carry important adjudication, tracing, request, and error-location information in R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances moving forward. They matter because R6 instances that use them cannot be represented in R4 without extensions, data loss, or profile-specific mapping. Some additions, such as `decision`, `reviewOutcome`, and `error.expression`, may be operationally significant.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping decision, review-outcome, request-link, trace, or error-location data can impair adjudication audit, remediation, and payer/provider reconciliation.

justification.inferredGoal: Model information that R4 ClaimResponse could not express directly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are additive optional R6 elements, so they do not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional elements is the normal backwards-compatible way for the base R6 resource to express information that R4 lacked. The migration problem is reverse conversion and information preservation, not avoidable R4-to-R6 instance breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for the R4-to-R6 direction because omitting these optional fields remains valid. Declining to add them would fail the R6 goal of representing trace, decision, review, supporting-info, request-link, tax, and error-expression data. Cross-version extensions are appropriate R6-to-R4 mitigations, but they are not a base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Optional additions are forward-compatible; R6-to-R4 export still needs extensions, loss policy, or rejection for data that R4 cannot represent natively.

evidence.detail: R6 adds trace numbers at header and nested item/addItem levels.
R6 adds a supportingInfo backbone with category, timing, value, and reason.
R6 adds reviewOutcome with decision, reason, preAuthRef, and preAuthPeriod and reuses it in detail/addItem structures.
R6 adds error expressions and marks them summary.
The corresponding R6-added element ids are absent from the R4 ClaimResponse snapshot.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment omits other required fields to focus on R6-only content. Native R4 fields cannot carry these values without extensions or external records.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 expands ClaimResponse substantially. These are not forward-breaking additions, but they are a serious round-trip and archival risk for systems that must consume R6 and emit R4 while preserving information.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances remain valid with respect to these optional additions. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy unless each new element is mapped to an extension, related resource, or implementation-guide-specific field. Strict R4 parsers will reject these unknown elements if they are left inline.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory which R6 additions are used by trading partners. Define cross-version extensions for values that must survive R4 export, especially trace numbers, decisions, review outcomes, supportingInfo, addItem request links, taxes, and error expressions. Add negative tests that ensure unknown R6 fields are not silently dropped when lossless conversion is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are backward-compatible in the R4-to-R6 direction and mostly unavoidable for new information needs. The compatible approach for R4 is explicit extensions or a documented lossy export mode.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Prioritize review based on actual payer/provider workflows because the prevalence of these new fields is unknown from core definitions alone.

findings.title: ClaimResponse.outcome required binding moved from remittance-outcome to claim-outcome with stable code values

binding.description: The result of the claim processing.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 outcome codes were `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial` from the remittance-outcome value set.

binding.description: The result of the claim processing.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem inspection found the same four code values in the old remittance-outcome and new claim-outcome systems; no terminology server expansion was run.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a new claim-outcome value set and code system canonical, while retaining the same apparent code values.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `ClaimResponse.outcome` is a primitive `code`, instances carry only values such as `complete`, and the inspected code values are unchanged. The main risk is terminology-service, enum-name, binding-canonical, and documentation logic that keys on the old value set or code system canonical.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Outcome drives workflow routing, but the actual primitive code values appear stable.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename terminology from remittance-oriented outcome to claim-outcome while preserving codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the primitive outcome code values appear stable, so this is terminology metadata/runtime churn rather than an R4-to-R6 instance break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Renaming the binding from remittance-outcome to claim-outcome is plausibly clearer for ClaimResponse, and the inspected primitive codes remain `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial`. Because instances carry only the code string, the base JSON compatibility impact is low; the main concern is terminology tooling and generated metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the old value set canonical would avoid metadata churn but would not accomplish the terminology rename. An official ConceptMap, alias, or terminology migration note would be useful mitigation for validators and code generators, but that is support metadata rather than a less-breaking base R6 design for the element itself.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The canonical rename can affect terminology caches, generated enum metadata, and documentation; ConceptMaps or aliases would mitigate migration but are not less-breaking base field designs.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is required to remittance-outcome version 4.0.1.
R6 binding is required to claim-outcome version 6.0.0-ballot4.
Local CodeSystems show the same four codes: queued, complete, error, partial.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON value transform appears necessary for the primitive code. Terminology metadata and generated enums may still need to update canonical names.

findings.narrativeMd: `ClaimResponse.outcome` changed its required value set canonical from remittance-outcome to claim-outcome. The four primitive code values inspected locally are stable, so this is not a hard instance break, but it is a terminology integration and code-generation migration note.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Existing JSON values such as `queued`, `complete`, `error`, and `partial` should remain valid. Systems that validate by canonical value set URL, generate enums from value set names, or store terminology-system metadata may need updates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update binding canonical references, generated enum metadata, terminology cache configuration, and tests that mention `remittance-outcome`. Treat the code values as preserved unless an official expansion or ConceptMap indicates otherwise.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the canonical without changing codes minimizes instance impact. An official ConceptMap or alias would further reduce runtime terminology risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium because local CodeSystems were inspected, but no official terminology expansion or ConceptMap was available.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition exists at the expected path with the same canonical URL, id, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag. The resource status changed from draft to active, which is not an instance-breaking identity change.
No local non-inherited ClaimResponse element changed its `isModifier` flag. Modifier-extension flag behavior inherited from base element definitions is out of scope.

No material local ClaimResponse-specific invariant change was found. Snapshot differences in `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and root `dom-*` constraints are inherited from base artifacts and excluded from findings.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value changes were found in the compared ClaimResponse snapshots.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex change on ClaimResponse-specific elements was identified beyond datatype-level primitive changes that are out of scope.
No local slicing changes were identified in the ClaimResponse snapshots.

Existing local reference targets such as `request`, `requestor`, `communicationRequest`, `insurance.coverage`, and `insurance.claimResponse` did not show material narrowing. Material new/widened targets are captured in findings for `subject`, `addItem.bodySite.site`, and R6 additions.

`ClaimResponse.error.code` changed to `isSummary=true`, and several R6-added elements such as `decision`, `statusReason`, `subject`, and `error.expression` are summary elements. These are noted as runtime/query awareness items rather than hard instance-breaking findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource maturity/status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical URL, id, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag remain stable. Status metadata does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and conformance documentation may treat active R6 content differently from draft R4 content.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several example bindings strengthened to preferred
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Preferred bindings guide terminology choice but do not make off-value-set codes invalid in the same way as required bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology validation dashboards may show stronger warnings or quality expectations for adjudication category, payment type, adjustment reason, and funds reserve codes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required status and use code values appear stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Local R4 and R6 CodeSystems for `fm-status` and `claim-use` contain the same inspected code values, though value set version URLs changed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enum metadata and terminology cache keys may need version updates even when instance code strings stay the same.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Error details are more visible in R6 summary views
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Changing or adding `isSummary` flags affects summary serialization/query behavior but does not invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients using `_summary` or generated summary projections should expect `error.code` and new `error.expression` to be included in R6 summary-oriented views.
